transcript:
Meeting header: Date/time: 2028-06-10 15:30 UTC | Duration: 63m | Location: Zoom | Recording: yes
Attendees: Jordan Ellis (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Logan Chu (Redwood CSM); Dana Park (Vanguard Head of MLOps), Miguel Santos (VP Engineering), Aisha Rahman (FinOps), Tom Becker (SRE)

Summary: Quick QBR-style checkpoint focused on usage trends, cost stability, and upcoming pilot choices for inference. Main threads: recent burst in embeddings, concern about sustained e2e latency for customer-facing features, tradeoffs between Hosted vs Dedicated, and KMS + audit log requirements for Private deployment. Agreed next steps and benchmarking plan.

Topics: usage trends; embedding burst; latency vs cost; dedicated capacity sizing; security/compliance (SOC2, KMS); timeline for pilot; ownership for action items

[00:00] Jordan: hey everyone thanks for joining, we'll keep this tight—agenda is usage, costs, reliability signals and a short pilot decision path, um 60 minutes ish. Dana, did I get that right?
[00:32] Dana: yeah thanks jordan, appreciate it. we've seen a 3x spike on embedding calls the last two weeks after we shipped compare feature, so FinOps is a bit sweaty, we need to understand how to cap cost without regressing UX.
[01:10] Aisha: yeah the invoices jumped, mostly during east coast mornings, and some weekends. what's our unit cost now on text and embedding calls with Redwood hosted?
[01:30] Jordan: current hosted blend is on the pricing sheet we sent last month — embeddings are roughly X units, text gen separate. i'll reattach the latest sheet after this call but rough order we saw in your account is about 1.8x than initial forecast due to the embeddings burst.
[02:05] Miguel: is that mostly because of query volume or because the models being used are higher-cost? we tested a larger model for better recall and maybe that's the driver.
[02:30] Priya: quick note, our runtime automatically routes to model variants when under load; but if you pinned to the higher LLM that increases token unit cost — also batching behavior changes with interactive patterns, so prefix repetition and short chats can be inefficient.
[03:05] Tom: from SRE side, the latency we see at 95th is creeping up during peak QPS. is that Redwood's autoscale policy or our client-side retries creating spikes?
[03:30] Priya: probably both — autoscale looks at GPU pool utilization and queued depth, but client spikes from retries make tail latency worse. we can recommend a client-side jitter/backoff and a small burst buffer in Dedicated to keep p95 under 400ms.
[04:12] Dana: can you explain Dedicated burst buffer? i've heard reserved capacity but not the "burst" config.
[04:30] Jordan: Dedicated = reserved GPU pools for you, predictable throughput. burst = temporary burst capacity purchased a la cart or via auto-burst policy for short windows of demand. it's cheaper than throwing in full extra nodes for 24/7.
[05:05] Aisha: okay but how does billing treat bursts vs reserved? is burst billed at a premium? we need clarity for FinOps modeling.
[05:30] Jordan: burst has a higher per-hour price than reserved, but because it's used infrequently it usually helps lower overall monthly cost vs overprovisioning reserved capacity. we'll send a cost scenario spreadsheet.
[06:00] Miguel: switching topics — security. We need encryption at rest with customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) and full audit logs. is that available in Private?
[06:30] Priya: yes Private supports customer KMS and HSM integrations; audit logs and longer retention can be configured. Hosted has envelope encryption and vetted controls, but Private gives you the keys. We also have SSO/SAML and RBAC in the console.
[07:05] Tom: do you provide per-token access logs or only aggregated metrics? our compliance folks want per-request audit trail for certain endpoints.
[07:30] Priya: we capture request-level metadata and can stream logs to your SIEM via secure transfer in Private. Hosted can provide logs but with sampling—we can go over exact retention SLA in the security docs.
[08:12] Dana: i'll need to loop in our security lead, i'll share contact details. question — any SOC2 evidence or ISO stuff you can share?
[08:30] Logan: yes we have SOC2 Type II and an ISO readiness pack; i'll drop the link after the call, plus a short checklist of what customers usually send to their auditors.
[09:00] Aisha: about the benchmark — can Redwood run a latency and cost test with our exact prompt set? that will help FinOps decide whether to go Hosted or Dedicated.
[09:30] Priya: absolutely. best is if you provide a 100-200 prompt sample and traffic profile (QPS distribution). we can run a 10k token pass sim and give p50/p95/p99 and cost per 1k tokens for both hosted and dedicated modes.
[10:05] Dana: ok we'll provide sample prompts — Tom will export traffic windows.
[10:30] Tom: I'll get the traffic CSV and typical retry rates, expect it by 6/14.
[11:00] Jordan: great. pilot timeline? if benchmarks look good, a 30-day pilot on Dedicated with a small reserved baseline + burst buffer feels reasonable.
[11:30] Miguel: we have Q3 compliance review on 7/10 so ideally pilot starts mid-June and we have final decision before the review.
[12:00] Aisha: mid-June start sounds good if we get costs by 6/15.
[12:30] Priya: technical note — for Dedicated we recommend a quantization profile and model variant that keeps cost within 30% of hosted while preserving 95% of quality for your rerank tasks. We'll propose two model configs in the benchmark results.
[13:05] Dana: any gotchas around KV cache when you move between models or versions? we saw a cache miss storm during a past rollout with another vendor.
[13:30] Priya: we do incremental KV migration and a warmup strategy; we also support graceful fallback to a compatible variant to avoid cold-start spikes. we'll include rollout playbook in the handoff doc.
[14:10] Miguel: contract questions — cancellation windows, data deletion guarantees post-contract?
[14:30] Jordan: standard is 30-day termination for pilot, data deletion clauses included with Private. We'll attach redlines we've done with similar customers.
[15:00] Aisha: please capture an explicit cost model in the spreadsheet: reserved baseline, burst hours, per-token, and estimated savings with batching and quantization.
[15:30] Jordan: noted — I'll include estimated savings scenarios.
[16:05] Dana: for the deep dive with SRE we want to go over network topologies — VPC peering options, private endpoints, and egress costs.
[16:30] Priya: we support VPC peering and private endpoints; egress depends on region and routing. we'll have our infra architect join the deep dive.
[17:00] Tom: can you give a rough p95 target we can expect on Dedicated for our load shape?
[17:30] Priya: with a small baseline and burst buffer, assuming GPU A100 family equivalent, p95 should be under 400ms for typical chat flows; embeddings p95 will be lower but depends on batch size. we'll validate in the benchmark.
[18:05] Miguel: one more — model rollouts and canarying. we need a rollback plan if quality drops post-deploy.
[18:30] Priya: we have canary/A-B layouts in the console, automatic fallback to prior variant on error thresholds, and eval hooks tied to your prompt sets for regression alerts.
[19:00] Dana: that evaluation hook sounds useful — can it run nightly on a held-out prompt set?
[19:30] Priya: yes, scheduler can run nightly checks and send regression alerts to Slack/email and the Console.
[20:00] Jordan: ok let's recap quickly — Redwood action: send updated pilot pricing and scenario sheet by 6/15; Priya runs the benchmark with your prompts and profile and returns results by 6/18; Vanguard action: Tom sends traffic CSV by 6/14; Dana to provide compliance contacts by 6/20.
[20:35] Aisha: all good. question — competitors, we are also evaluating Anthropic's embed pricing — any points to highlight versus them?
[21:00] Jordan: short answer: we focus on predictable per-token economics and stronger operational tooling for rollouts and private key control — Anthropic has product strengths too, but our differentiation is around production controls and cost levers like KV caching and configurable batching.
[21:40] Miguel: thanks — that helps finance frame the conversation.
[22:00] Logan: i'll drop the SOC2 pack, pilot comparison and a short playbook after this call.
[22:20] Dana: thanks team — expect our items this week.
